articles.title: Quantum Error-Reduction Software Maker Q-CTRL Raises $290 Million Series C
articles.snippet: Quantum Error-Reduction Software Maker Q-CTRL Raises $290 Million Series C Wowtale
articles.text:
Money is pouring into companies that build quantum computers. Oratomic raised a $475 million Series B in October, and Universal Quantum closed a Series A of more than $100 million. But whether qubits are made from neutral atoms or trapped ions, the problem is the same: they are sensitive to noise and make errors mid-calculation. Q-CTRL , an Australian company that sells software to reduce those errors, said it raised a $290 million Series C (A$415 million). It says the round makes it the newest quantum unicorn, though it did not disclose a valuation.
Software that makes other companies’ chips usable
Q-CTRL does not build quantum computers. Founded in 2017 by Michael Biercuk , a University of Sydney physicist, it sells software that helps machines built by other companies run better. It pitches a hardware-agnostic design that is not tied to any one qubit technology.
It has two main products. Fire Opal is cloud software that automatically shortens the quantum circuits a developer writes, maps them onto a chip according to each machine’s error profile and corrects measurement errors before returning results. It runs on IBM’s quantum service, IonQ and Rigetti systems and Amazon Braket, among others, and the company claims it can run circuits up to 10 times deeper on the same hardware. Boulder Opal is for those who build or operate quantum computers. Even after it is switched on, a quantum computer needs its control signals tuned qubit by qubit, and the product automates that calibration and upkeep without a team of physicists. It supports superconducting and semiconductor spin-qubit machines, with trapped-ion and neutral-atom support available on request, the company says. Its target customers are chipmakers and data center and HPC operators. In computing, the company also claims a 3,000x speedup in materials discovery for the energy sector.
The third business pairs software with sensors. Ironstone Opal is a navigation system for places where GPS is unavailable or jammed. It measures tiny variations in the Earth’s magnetic field and matches them against a magnetic map to find its position. The company builds the quantum magnetometers itself, and AI software filters out the magnetic interference the aircraft generates. The company says the system is 100 times better than the best alternative, but in its published flight trial it reported up to 50 times lower positioning uncertainty than an inertial navigation system. It says Ironstone Opal is being deployed on commercial aircraft with Airbus, on autonomous platforms with Lockheed Martin and on drones. All performance figures come from the company.
Led by Salesforce Ventures, expanded twice
Salesforce Ventures led the round, with Bullhound Capital and Affinity Partners named as headline participants. The company says it expanded the round twice to meet investor demand and calls it the largest raise by a software-focused quantum company. Q-CTRL expanded its Series B to $113 million in October 2024.
New investors are Affinity Partners, AMD Ventures, EDGE Group, MPower Partners, Australia’s National Reconstruction Fund Corporation and SPARX Asset Management. Returning investors are Alpha Edison, Alumni Ventures, Bullhound Capital, DCVC, In-Q-Tel, Lockheed Martin Ventures, Main Sequence, Ridgeline, Salesforce Ventures, Salus Ventures and Square Peg. Crypto financing announcements have totaled approximately $408.55 million across nine disclosed transactions during Nov. 7–13, 2026, led by a reported $270 million commitment to the bank-backed stablecoin venture Project Faro.
Summary
Nine disclosed financings totaled $408.55 million, including bank commitments and two public token sales.
Project Faro drew approximately $270 million in reported commitments for five years of operations.
Index Industries raised $50 million in seed funding led by Lightspeed Venture Partners.
Alta secured a $47.5 million Series A, bringing its cumulative funding to $80 million.
Project Faro, Index and Alta accounted for nearly 90% of the disclosed weekly total.
The tally includes corporate funding commitments and public token sales alongside venture rounds. Four further announcements covered cumulative or undisclosed funding.
DefiLlama’s funding database provided the weekly inventory, with company announcements, investor disclosures and reporting used to check transaction details.
Project Faro leads crypto financing with $270 million commitment
Goldman Sachs, Citigroup, Santander and Deutsche Bank were among institutions committing around $270 million to a stablecoin venture , as crypto.news reported, citing Bloomberg’s Nov. 10 report.
Known as Project Faro, the proposed business would use the capital to cover five years of operating costs. The figure represents committed corporate financing, with no announcement that the full amount has been paid.
The 21-member consortium expects to establish its issuer in the United States. Its stated launch window is the first half of 2027, beginning with a dollar stablecoin intended for payments and digital asset settlement. A euro token is planned later.

Its first planned application is USHP, issued separately by British Virgin Islands-based USHP Limited. The issuer plans an Ethereum release in 2026 and a Solana expansion in 2027.
The announcement states that the referenced securities are unregistered in the United States and cannot be offered to U.S. persons without registration or an applicable exemption.

articles.text:
Attorney General Mike Hilgers announces $183.5 Million multistate settlement with Rent-to-Own finance company Acima Digital, LLC
Courtesy Photo
November 15th, 2026 | Nebraska Attorney General’s Office
Lincoln – Attorney General Mike Hilgers announced a $183.5 million multistate settlement with Acima Digital, LLC, and its parent company, Acima Holdings, LLC. The settlement includes $43 million in consumer restitution, $10.5 million to participating states, and $130 million in lease balance reductions. Nebraska will receive more than $292,608.42 in restitution and $593,465.05 in lease forgiveness for Nebraska consumers.
Acima, a rent-to-own financing company that partners with Nebraska retailers, was accused of misleading consumers about the terms and costs of its rental-purchase agreements. Forty-three states alleged that Acima advertised 90-day payoff programs without clearly disclosing that consumers were automatically placed in 12-month agreements and could end up paying twice the advertised cash price. The company also allegedly misrepresented its services as traditional credit, marked up merchandise prices, and made it difficult for consumers to return merchandise and end agreements.
Under the settlement, Acima must improve retail partner training, provide clearer advertising and contract disclosures, stop marking up merchandise prices, allow consumers to return merchandise without obstruction, and properly address delivery, damage, and repair issues. The company also cannot report rental-purchase agreements to the three major credit bureaus for five years.
Consumers eligible for restitution or lease forgiveness do not need to take action. The settlement administrator will contact consumers receiving restitution, while Acima will notify those eligible for lease forgiveness.

Novo Holdings-Backed Windward Bio Raises $175m in US IPO as Biotech Listings Gather Pace
November 13, 2026
|
by
Samuel Nwite
|
0
Windward Bio has raised $175 million in its US initial public offering, adding to a growing pipeline of healthcare and biotechnology companies tapping public markets as listings in other sectors face pressure from economic uncertainty.
The Basel, Switzerland-based drug developer sold approximately 10.3 million shares at $17 each, within its marketed range of $16 to $18. Its shares are scheduled to begin trading on Friday on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol WWB.
The offering gives Windward fresh capital to advance its experimental antibody medicines for serious respiratory and dermatological diseases, with its lead programme targeting conditions that affect millions of patients worldwide. The company is backed by Novo Holdings, alongside other healthcare investors, and has attracted a $50 million commitment from French pharmaceutical group Sanofi.

Sanofi agreed to purchase $50 million in shares and pre-funded warrants through a private placement, providing Windward with an additional source of institutional backing as it enters the public market. The investment also gives the pharmaceutical group exposure to a biotechnology company developing treatments in areas where demand for new therapies remains significant.
Windward’s lead candidate, WIN378, is being developed for asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, or COPD. The antibody is designed to block a protein involved in airway inflammation, an approach intended to address an underlying biological mechanism contributing to both conditions.
The programme will be central to the company’s development strategy as it moves into the public market. However, WIN378 remains an experimental medicine, and its commercial prospects will depend on clinical results, regulatory approvals and its ability to demonstrate meaningful benefits over existing treatments.
Led by founder and chief executive Luca Santarelli, Windward has raised $310 million in equity financing from Novo Holdings and other healthcare investors, including OrbiMed, Blue Owl and RTW Investments.
Santarelli has previously built biotechnology businesses that attracted substantial acquisition interest from larger pharmaceutical companies. VectivBio, one of his earlier ventures, was acquired by Ironwood Pharmaceuticals for $1.2 billion in 2023. Pfizer acquired another company he was associated with, Therachon, in 2019 for $810 million.
That history provides Windward with a management team familiar with biotechnology development and the commercial pressures facing companies seeking to bring new medicines to market. However, previous acquisitions do not guarantee that its current drug candidates will achieve similar outcomes.
The company’s IPO also underscores the importance of specialist healthcare investors in financing drug development. Biotechnology companies often require substantial capital over several years before generating commercial revenue, as clinical trials, regulatory submissions, and manufacturing preparations result in costs well ahead of product launches.

articles.text:
Before Trump Eased Nvidia Chip Exports to China, He Bought $160 Million in Stock, Raising Conflict-of-Interest Questions
Add preferred source
1
U.S. President Donald Trump has been revealed to have purchased $1 million to $5 million worth of Nvidia stock (approximately NT$33 million to NT$160 million) just before rescinding the Biden administration's AI chip export controls, and to have made at least three additional purchases of $250,000 to $500,000 each after opening H200 chip sales to China. An anti-corruption organization is questioning the intersection of policy shifts and personal financial interests. The controversy deepened after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned amid suspicions of involvement with an alleged Chinese spy. Democrats have launched an investigation, leaving Nvidia's China business prospects facing dual policy and political uncertainties.
Key Elements
Donald Trump Nvidia Jensen Huang Alice Huang DeKleptocracy U.S. Department of Commerce H200 chips AI Diffusion Framework Megaspeed The Guardian Council on Foreign Relations
U.S. President Donald Trump has been revealed to have made large purchases of Nvidia stock on the eve of rescinding the previous administration's AI chip export controls, triggering strong questions about the intersection of policy and personal financial interests. According to an analysis by anti-corruption organization DeKleptocracy of Trump's public financial disclosure filings, Trump purchased $1 million to $5 million worth of Nvidia shares (approximately NT$33 million to NT$160 million) just days before scrapping the Biden administration's "Framework for Artificial Intelligence Diffusion" in May of last year.
The policy had originally established tiered management of AI chip exports based on each country's diplomatic and security relationship with the United States, with allies such as South Korea placed in a relatively permissive category, while China, Russia, and North Korea faced the strictest export blockades. The core purpose of the Biden administration's framework was to slow China's acquisition of advanced computing power and thereby its ability to build up its own AI capabilities. The Trump administration decided to scrap the entire framework on the grounds that it hindered American corporate innovation, imposed unnecessary regulatory burdens, and effectively relegated dozens of countries to "second-tier" status in a way that could damage diplomatic relations.
The timing overlap makes this transaction particularly sensitive. Had the framework actually taken effect, Nvidia's shipments to China—a market that once contributed about a quarter of its sales—would have been significantly constrained. After Trump announced the rescission of the controls, Nvidia's stock price promptly rose. The disclosure filings also show that Trump simultaneously purchased shares in tech giants including Apple, Meta, and Microsoft, rather than betting solely on Nvidia.
The controversy does not end there. In December 2025, Trump further announced that Nvidia would be allowed to sell H200 chips to approved customers in China, and the U.S. Department of Commerce formally granted approval in January 2026. The H200 was one of Nvidia's most advanced products at the time, with experts estimating its performance at roughly six times that of the chips China could obtain at the time. MaxCyte: $151.8 Million Akron Bio Acquisition Expands Cell Therapy Platform
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 11:44 AM
MaxCyte: $151.8 Million Akron Bio Acquisition Expands Cell Therapy Platform
MaxCyte has agreed to acquire Akron BioProducts from affiliates of Arcline Investment Management for $151.8 million. The transaction is expected to close before the end of 2026, subject to customary conditions.
Akron Bio supplies Good Manufacturing Practice-grade reagents and ancillary materials used across cell therapy manufacturing. Its products include cytokines, growth factors, human plasma-derived materials, specialty media, and other consumables.
The acquisition will expand MaxCyte beyond its historical focus on nonviral cell engineering. Akron’s products are used in both viral and nonviral workflows at stages ranging from cell expansion through cryopreservation.
The combined company’s technologies are incorporated into five commercially approved therapies and support more than 100 clinical programs. Both businesses maintain drug master files referenced in customers’ regulatory submissions, creating long-term connections to validated manufacturing processes.
Akron is expected to produce approximately $28 million in 2026 revenue and between $7 million and $8 million of EBITDA. MaxCyte expects the acquisition to nearly double its revenue base, increase recurring consumables revenue, and accelerate its path toward profitability.
The companies have limited customer overlap despite serving similar biopharmaceutical markets. MaxCyte therefore expects to use its commercial infrastructure to introduce Akron products to additional customers and pursue cross-selling opportunities.
The buyer projects that Akron’s positive cash flow will help reduce the combined company’s annual cash burn to less than $10 million in 2027. MaxCyte expects to hold approximately $40 million to $45 million of cash when the transaction closes.
The consideration consists of $105 million in cash, subject to adjustments, 20,639,733 MaxCyte shares valued at approximately $26.8 million, and $20 million of guaranteed deferred payments. The deferred amount will be paid in two $10 million installments in January 2028 and January 2029.
MaxCyte has also secured a credit facility of up to $75 million from MidCap Financial, consisting of a $55 million term loan and a $20 million revolver. It plans to draw $20 million from the term loan and $2 million from the revolver at closing.
Akron will continue operating under its existing brand, with its management team and employees remaining part of the combined organization.
KEY QUOTES
“The acquisition of Akron marks an exciting new chapter for MaxCyte. This acquisition represents a significant step forward for us, expanding our presence across the viral and non-viral cell therapy development and manufacturing workflow, while projecting to nearly double our revenue base and accelerate our path to profitability. From day one, Akron provides us with an established portfolio of clinical and commercial programs supported by Akron’s DMFs and reagents. By bringing together two highly complementary businesses, we are diversifying our revenue base, increasing our mix of recurring revenue and expanding our exposure to the growth of commercially approved cell therapies, positioning MaxCyte for more durable near- and long-term growth. articles.title: Vumedi Raises $140M Series B, Oakland Health Tech
articles.snippet: Vumedi Raises $140M Series B, Oakland Health Tech Hoodline
articles.text:
555 12th St. — Oakland Street Scene
Google Street View
An Oakland health-tech company has raised $140 million in a new funding round. Vumedi, which builds an AI-powered learning platform for physicians, has raised $140 million in Series B funding, with plans to pour the money into talent, research and development, product development and outreach as it expands its clinical learning tools.
The investment came from Oak HC/FT, according to FinSMEs , which reported the round. Vumedi is led by founder and CEO Roman Giverts, and the company describes its platform as a tool that connects clinicians with specialists and peers so they can learn procedures, evaluate treatments and navigate complex cases, the outlet reports.
What the Platform Actually Does
At the center of Vumedi's pitch is scale paired with AI. The platform uses artificial intelligence to turn more than 100,000 physician-led videos and nearly 5,000 podcast episodes, spanning more than 21 medical specialties, into what the company calls an on-demand clinical resource, per the same report. Rather than leaving clinicians to sift through hours of footage, the system synthesizes multiple expert perspectives and links directly to time-stamped segments within videos.
The company says its platform now serves more than 150,000 NPI-verified clinicians and generated over 56 million minutes of learning over the past 12 months. Back in a 2018 interview, Giverts described Vumedi's mission as helping physicians make the best care decisions through what he called unbiased video education in an interview with MPO-mag.com . That same article reported the platform then had roughly 250,000 physician users and 20,000 videos contributed by more than 5,000 healthcare organizations and professionals, including partnerships with 150 hospitals and conferences such as Cleveland Clinic, Mayo Clinic and Johns Hopkins.
Funding Figures Don't All Line Up
Not every account of Vumedi's fundraising history tells the same story. A snippet from 01net referenced a $104 million investment from Oak HC/FT, though it's unclear from that report whether it describes the same financing as the newly reported $140 million round or a separate transaction. Separately, CB Insights lists Vumedi's most recent funding round as a $79.98 million Series B dated May 22, 2025, and puts the company's total raised at $82.08 million across four rounds. The available reporting does not reconcile these differing figures with the $140 million sum reported this week.
Part of a Broader AI Health-Tech Wave
Vumedi's raise lands amid a broader uptick in digital-health investment. Companies in the sector raised $7.4 billion in the first half of 2026, up roughly $1 billion from the same period in 2025, according to Fierce Healthcare . The outlet counted 244 completed deals in that window, with $4.2 billion invested in the first quarter and $3.2 billion in the second.
A notable share of that capital came in the form of megadeals. Nineteen companies raised 20 financings of at least $100 million in the first half of 2026, representing 45 percent of all capital invested, Fierce Healthcare reported, citing deals that included AI radiology company Aidoc's $150 million raise.
